page: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor and powered by custom AWS Graviton processors based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. The instance features 96 dedicated physical CPU cores without hyperthreading running at 3.3 GHz, 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 96 MB L3 cache. It is provisioned with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration includes AES cryptography support, while x86 vector extensions are omitted. The server contains no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote network-attached storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark tests, the c9g.24xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core scalability due to its high physical core density. Its stress-ng multi-core CPU score reaches 192014.4 alongside a PassMark CPU score of 77220.39 and an extended instructions score of 129079.05. Memory throughput is highlighted by a cached read bandwidth of 13912.96 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 4603.51. In workload-specific benchmarks, the server achieves 269.45 million SET operations per second in Redis, 198.56 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and a PassMark database operations score of 57730.61. Single-core performance is moderate with a stress-ng score of 2007.4, but multi-threaded processing excels, reaching 1131.71 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and 4506.32 tokens/sec for small LLM prompt processing.

By leveraging dedicated ARMv9 physical cores without hyperthreading overhead, c9g.24xlarge provides reliable compute execution and high core density. The instance offers strong compute-per-resource efficiency for parallel workloads, though its lack of bundled local NVMe storage requires external disk provision, and x86 software must be compiled for arm64 target architecture. The 2.0 GB per core memory allocation constrains memory-intensive workloads, but the server performs efficiently across scale-out network and compute services. Best-fit workloads include high-concurrency web serving, key-value cache nodes like Redis, parallel data compression pipelines, database transaction processing, and CPU-based LLM prompt execution.
